keyVerseText: For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD; I will set him in safety from him that puffeth at him. puffeth: or, would ensnare him
rootMeaning: The root of אֲנָקָה (ʼănâqâh) is the verb אָנַק (ʼânaq), which fundamentally means to cry out or groan, often with an intense emotional or physical expression such as a shriek or lamentation. This root conveys not just any form of crying but a deep, heartfelt outcry that can be both audible and expressive of distress. The literal sense of this root enriches the English glosses by emphasizing the intensity and urgency behind the act of crying or groaning, beyond a mere tear or quiet sigh.
usageInScripture: The word אֲנָקָה appears four times in the Hebrew Scriptures, consistently associated with expressions of distress such as crying, groaning, sighing, or lamentation. Its translations vary slightly — from 'for the sighing' and 'Let the sighing' to 'the groaning' and 'with crying out' — but all maintain a focus on a vocal or emotional response to hardship or oppression. This consistency highlights the word's role in conveying the depth of human suffering and the earnestness of the plea or complaint expressed.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲנָקָה in its original sense of a profound cry or groan deepens our appreciation for the biblical portrayal of human suffering and dependence on God. It reminds believers that God is attentive not only to superficial complaints but to the sincere, often anguished cries of the needy and oppressed. This word underscores the biblical truth that God rises to deliver those who express their distress to Him, reflecting His compassion and justice. In Christ, who Himself groaned and cried out in suffering, believers find a Savior who fully understands and enters into human pain, offering hope and salvation.
keyVerseReflection: Psalm 12:5 says, 'For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, now will I arise, saith the LORD.' The use of אֲנָקָה here as 'sighing' conveys a deep, heartfelt expression of distress from those in need. This word enriches the verse by highlighting the intensity of the needy's plea, assuring us that God hears these sincere cries and promises to act on their behalf. It powerfully illustrates God's readiness to rescue those who earnestly call upon Him in their affliction.
